That as the services print is a 5-month high with the composite print being a 8-month high.

Of note, output and new orders rose at strongest rates since last November as inflation cools.

The July expansion was broad-based amid further growth in the services sector as well as a more sustained uplift in the manufacturing side.

Germany posted its first rise in private sector output since March, while both Italy and Spain saw stronger rates of growth.

Looking to price pressures, the rates of both input cost and output charge inflation dropped in July.

And adding to that, prices set for euro area goods and services were lifted by the smallest margin since March.

All that being said, the pace of both input and output price inflation were elevated relative to the survey average historically (chart below).
